VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` also marks a tool available when the tool times out. Evidence: `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., stderr="TIMEOUT", returncode=-1)` on timeout; each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"` and otherwise returns `[]`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. This is the same availability root cause, not just missing binaries.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is silently lossy in fix evaluation too, not just health scan. `_count_tool_issues()` calls runners and returns `len(diags)`. When `_run_tool()` times out, runners return `[]`, so pre/post counts become zero and `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE`/`NEUTRAL` despite no tool evidence. Downstream this can wrongly mark findings as `verified=True` in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, activating the bug-closed gate on unevaluated fixes.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or project context, so the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” can evaluate the patched file against the unpatched codebase and produce misleading SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts. Evidence: it writes only the target file into `TemporaryDirectory` as `patched_path = tmpdir/basename(target_path)`, then runs `run_pyright([patched_path])`, `run_ruff([patched_path])`, and `run_bandit([patched_path])` on that lone file. For any fix whose validity depends on sibling modules, package-relative imports, or project config, the patched file is analyzed out of package context while the rest of the real source tree remains unchanged. This violates the module docstring promise: “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)” implies evaluating the fix in a temporary copy of the source tree, not a detached single-file artifact.
FOLLOW: The downstream effect is silently wrong fix verdicts, which is HIGH in this PoC because fix verification feeds closure logic. A valid fix can be marked harmful/unevaluable due to broken detached imports, and an invalid fix can be marked neutral because only the edited file is checked while dependent files remain real and untouched. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface: in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, findings with `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` are marked `verified=True`; later NK dedup treats `verified` findings as CLOSED. A false SAFE/NEUTRAL here can suppress future reports of a still-open bug, while a false HARMFUL blocks the first sufficient fix from closing the issue.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the full relevant source tree (or at minimum all `source_paths` preserving relative paths) into the temp directory, apply the patch to the copied target file there, and run tools with `cwd` set to that temp root against the copied path. This preserves package/import context while still avoiding modification of real source.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` runs any provided `test_cmd` verbatim in the temp directory without rebasing file arguments to the sandbox, so tests typically execute against real-source paths or fail to find the intended targets. Evidence: after creating `tmpdir`, the code calls `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)` unchanged. If `test_cmd` contains repository-relative paths like `bench/tests/` or a specific source file, those arguments still point outside the sandbox layout because only one patched file was copied into `tmpdir`. `cwd=tmpdir` changes the working directory, but it does not rewrite command arguments. The function therefore does not actually test the patched sandbox in the common case.
FOLLOW: This makes the “tests_passed” signal unreliable and can silently misclassify fixes. A passing result may be exercising the real repository instead of the patched sandbox; a failing result may be just a missing-path artifact. Downstream, `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats `tests_passed is False` as HARMFUL and `tests_passed is True` as evidence for SAFE. That directly affects Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL fixes mark findings verified and can close the bug. In practice, the endocrine layer can report that a fix was sandbox-tested when no sandboxed test actually occurred.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when building the sandbox, map any path-like entries in `test_cmd` from original repo paths to their copied equivalents inside the temp root, and run the rewritten command there. If command rebasing is not possible, skip tests and return `tests_passed=None` with an explicit apply/test error instead of pretending the sandbox test ran.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify fixes as SAFE when one tool regresses and another improves, because it sums net deltas across unrelated tool classes and only checks the total. Evidence: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net > 0` ⇒ HARMFUL, `< 0` ⇒ SAFE. A fix that introduces one new Bandit security issue (`+1`) but removes two Ruff warnings (`-2`) yields `-1` and is marked SAFE. The docstring says “SAFE: no new issues introduced,” which the implementation violates.
FOLLOW: This is a silently wrong verdict, which is HIGH because the endocrine layer is the sole programmatic gate for fix verification. A security or type regression can be masked by unrelated lint improvements, leading Stage 4 of `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` to set `verified=True` on a harmful fix. Once verified, NK’s bug-closed gate can suppress future rediscovery. This crosses both defect classification and closure interfaces, not just local reporting.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — mark a fix HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only consider SAFE when at least one metric improves and none regress.
VERIFIED: TRUE

VERDICT: EXTEND C0005 | The dead/partial feature surface includes fix evaluation semantics, not just defect categories/tool claims. The module advertises “sandbox-test proposed fixes (SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL)” and “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)”, but current implementation copies only one file and does not rebase `test_cmd`, so the end-to-end sandbox feature only partially fires.
